title: 44 Creek Bridge Failure
description: 44 creek bridge is closed effective July 28, 2026 due to damage/deficiencies identified by a Federal Highway inspection team. This bridge is north of 44 Camp, approximately 7 miles south of the Redwood Creek trailhead and about 1 mile north of the Tall Trees river crossing. While all trails remain open in the area, but this bridge has failed. Crossing this ravine is dangerous and no advised. Alternative routes to 44 Camp will add at least 3.5 miles from Redwood Creek Trailhead.

title: Declaration 250 Event: July 31- August 2
description: For information on the Declaration 250 Event please visit: https://lakeerieheritage.org/

title: Fort Charlotte Campground Temporarily Closed Due to Wildfire Conditions
description: Grand Portage National Monument is temporarily closing the Fort Charlotte Campground effective immediately due to high fire danger and active wildfires across northeast Minnesota. This proactive closure is being issued to protect the safety and well-being of visitors, staff, and nearby communities as wildfire activity continues to create unpredictable and hazardous conditions. Fort Charlotte Campground reopens July 30. Campfire Ban remains in effect. Approved camp stoves only.

title: Mountain Road Status – CLOSED to Pedestrians
description: The paved Mountain Road is currently CLOSED to pedestrians, cyclists, and personal vehicles. Road work and any future closures will follow a weather‑dependent contractor schedule and may be announced on short notice. We will post updates as the project continues.

title: Water Unavailable at Au Sable Light Station
description: Water is unavailable at the Au Sable Light Station through 7/31.

title: Construction Activity at Meyers Beach; Visitor and Kayak Access Maintained
description: Construction has begun on the Meyers Beach Access Path Project. Access to the beach and parking lot will remain open, but visitors should expect construction noise and closed lawn areas for staging. Kayak groups should move gear directly to the beach to reduce congestion. The project will upgrade the existing staircase to include a universally designed path, improving access to the beach and kayak launch for all visitors.

title: No potable water available at Summit Campgrounds
description: Potable water is currently unavailable at both Summit campgrounds. Staff is working to restore it as soon as possible. Non-potable water is available.

title: Stage 2 Burn Restrictions
description: All campfires are prohibited. Devices using pressurized liquid or gas (stoves, grills or lanterns) that include shut-off valves are permitted when used in an area at least three feet or more from flammable material such as grasses or pine needles. Smoking is only allowed in an enclosed vehicle.

title: Visitor Center Restrooms Closed Until Further Notice
description: As of Tuesday, July 28, 2026, the restrooms at the White Sands National Park visitor center are closed until further notice. The closest restrooms to the visitor center are vault toilets at Dune Life Nature Trail, two and a half miles past the entrance station into the park. We apologize for the inconvenience.

title: Single-Lane Closures on Gatlinburg Spur
description: The park will conduct single-lane closures on the Gatlinburg Spur from July 27-30 to complete essential maintenance. Northbound lane closures are scheduled from July 27 through July 28, and southbound lane closures are scheduled July 29 through July 30. The closures will take place from 7 a.m. to 3:30 p.m. each day

title: Grand View Point Closed for Construction Weekdays July 27 to Oct 1
description: Grand View Point Overlook, Grand View Point Trail, and 0.3 mi (0.5 km) of park road is closed Monday to Thursday. The closure applies to all uses, including vehicles, tour buses, motorcycles, bikes, & hikers. Parking is open but limited Friday to Sunday.

title: Shafer Trail Closed
description: Shafer Trail Road is temporarily closed due to flooding damage.

title: Route 252 Closed between Route 23 and Covered Bridge - Resuming July 13
description: PennDOT Drainage Crew is replacing eight drainage pipes along Route 252 between Route 23 and the Knox Covered Bridge on Yellow Springs Road. Work is scheduled to resume on Monday July 13 and continue until completed. Daily daytime road closures will be in effect until project completion. All traffic will be detoured during working hours. Motorists are encouraged to plan ahead, allow additional travel time, and follow posted detour routes.

title: Library Lane Closed to All Pedestrian and Vehicular Traffic
description: Library Lane is closed to all pedestrian and vehicular traffic. Please view map to see pedestrian trail detour.

title: Lower Cliff Dwelling Trail Closed due to Extreme Heat Warning.
description: The Lower Cliff Dwelling trail will be closed Thursday, July 30 to Sunday, August 2nd. The trail will reopen Monday August 3rd at 8:00 a.m.

title: Osprey Falls Trail Temporary Closure
description: The Osprey Falls Trail, located south of Mammoth Hot Springs near Bunsen Peak, will be temporarily closed for critical trail repair work July 28–Aug. 4 from 8 a.m.–4 p.m. On July 30–31, the trail will be closed all day. The Old Bunsen Peak Road will remain open during repair work.

title: Traffic Delays - Yellowstone River Bridge
description: Expect up to 30-minute delays on the Yellowstone River Bridge, near Tower Junction, while crews perform paving operations. Crews will work during the day until Aug. 7, and at night Aug. 9-15. Dates and times are subject to change based on weather.

title: Their Space, Your Safety
description: Animals in Yellowstone are wild and dangerous. Stay at least 100 yards (91 m) from bears/wolves/cougars and 25 yards (23 m) from bison/elk/all other wildlife. Carry bear spray (even on short walks) and know how to use it—you can rent/purchase/recycle it at several locations in the park.

title: Park Rivers and Streams Closed to Fishing Daily from 2 p.m. to Sunrise
description: All park rivers and streams are closed to fishing daily from 2 p.m. to sunrise due to high water temperatures and low stream flows. Additionally, the Madison, Firehole, and Gibbon (downstream of Norris Campground) rivers are fully closed to fishing. These closures will remain in effect until conditions improve to protect the park’s native and wild trout fisheries.

title: Fort Pickens Area Water Boil Notice
description: All the drinking water in the Fort Pickens Area is under boil water notice until furthur notice.

title: Bridge to Maryland Heights & C&O Canal CLOSED
description: The NPS is rehabilitating the stairway connecting the Goodloe Byron Memorial Footbridge to the C&O Canal NHP towpath. The stairway will be CLOSED beginning July 27 for approximately one month while crews install the new stairwell. A shuttle will run between C&O Canal Lock 34 and Harpers Ferry National Historical Park Visitor Center. This will impact access to Maryland Heights, the Appalachian NST, and the Potomac Heritage NST.

title: Towpath Trail closed between Frazee House and Station Road
description: Due to hazardous conditions, the Towpath Trail is closed between Frazee House and Station Road Bridge Trailhead until further notice. There is no detour available. Please plan accordingly.

title: No water available in restrooms at Butte Lake campgrounds
description: Currently, no water is available in the restrooms at the Butte Lake campgrounds. Work is underway to restore it. Pit toilets are available.

title: Fort Nonsense Remains Closed
description: Due to conditions from the 7/3 storms, Fort Nonsense remains closed.

title: Jockey Hollow Outer Blue Loop and a Section of Primrose Trail Closed
description: Following storms on 7/3/2026, many park trails were closed due to blowdown of trees and hazardous conditions. As of 7/27/2026 most trails are passable. The Mount Kimble Trail (Outer Blue Loop) remains closed as well as a section of the Primrose Trail (Red Trail). Please check in at the Visitor Center for more information and take caution as summer storms continue to cause tree falls. Report any fallen trees to a Park Ranger.

title: Passaic River Bridge Trail (Teal Trail) Closed
description: The Passaic River Bridge Trail is closed between Tempe Wick Road and the Cross Estate in the New Jersey Brigade area due to construction of a new bridge.

title: Upcoming Closure of Billy Mitchell Airport for Repaving Project
description: Beginning August 3, Cape Hatteras National Seashore will close the Billy Mitchell Airport (HSE) to accommodate a runway pavement rehabilitation project. The project will provide full resurfacing of paved areas, new reflective paint, and new tie-downs and anchors, improving visitor safety and enhancing the overall visitor experience.

title: North Union Avenue Closed for Repairs
description: North Union Avenue is closed to vehicular and pedestrian traffic for repairs. Entering this construction area is prohibited. This work is to repair severe weather damage in 2020. The remainder of the park and tour road are open.

title: Mason's Branch Road Closure
description: Mason's Branch Road will be closed for necessary safety repairs from 07/29/26 through around 08/20/26. Check back for updates.

title: Hurricane Ridge Rd Closed 7am -12pm on Sunday 8/2
description: Hurricane Ridge Road will be closed at the Heart of the Hills gate from 7am–12pm on Sunday, 8/2 for the “Ride the Hurricane” bicycle event. No vehicles may exit the Hurricane Ridge parking lot after 7am. Please leave Hurricane Ridge Parking lot before 7am or plan to remain until the road reopens at 12pm.

title: Construction in the South End of the Park
description: Construction projects underway. Moose-Wilson Road between Murie Ranch and LS Rockefeller Preserve closed 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. July 28-July 30. Expect delays of 45 minutes in both directions all other times. No roadside parking on Moose-Wilson Road. Taggart Trail detour in place. Menor's Ferry Road closed weekdays. Mormon Row area open with some construction activity.

title: Monsoon Season & Flash Floods
description: Heavy rains can cause sudden flooding, especially in canyons and washes. Do not drive or hike through flood waters. Get to high ground and wait for floods to subside. Some roads may close temporarily; closures are posted at the visitor center.

title: Crews Responding to Lightning-Caused Mt. Tom Creek Fire
description: The lightning-caused Mt. Tom Creek Fire is burning on a remote mountain slope on the west side of Olympic National Park. Firefighters are using indirect confinement tactics as part of a full-suppression strategy. Backpackers are encouraged to consider alternative routes to the Hoh River Trail should fire activity increase. There are no evacuation orders or closures.

title: Loop A of the campground will be closed (noon) August 6-August 14.
description: Loop A of the campground will be closed (noon) August 6-August 14.

title: The campground will be closed (noon) August 9-August 13.
description: The whole campground which includes both loop A & loop B will be closed (noon) August 9-August 13.

title: Sturgis Motorcycle Rally Parking Change
description: The Sturgis Motorcycle Rally occurs Aug 10-13 at Devils Tower. During this time parking is extremely limited. Motorcycles and handicap vehicles can park at the top of the hill in the paved parking all day. A small dirt parking lot is available at the top of the hill as well. Once the dirt parking fills all vehicles that are not motorcycles or handicap vehicles must park in the picnic/campground/ long vehicle parking and take a shuttle up to the visitor center.

title: Sheep Rock Unit Closed due to Shingle Fire
description: Due to threats from the Shingle Fire which started on July 23 and is currently estimated at approximately 11,140 acres, the Grant County Sheriff’s Office has issued a Level 2 Evacuation order for the zone that includes the Thomas Condon Visitor Center of John Day Fossil Beds National Monument, and a Level 3 Evacuation order for the portion of Sheep Rock south of Picture Gorge. An Emergency Closure of the Sheep Rock Unit has been implemented to protect public safety.

title: Trail update 7/25/26
description: Most trails are open and ready for the public. Those that remain closed are the Charleston Road/ Goudey Trail past the Cherokee Path and the portion of Cherokee Path between the stockade fort and the Charleston Road.

title: Bicycles and Pedestrians now allowed on Volcano Road
description: Capulin Volcano Highway is now a roadway shared by multiple users that include vehicles, hikers, bikers, walkers and runners. Dogs on a minimum 6-foot leash are also allowed on the roadway. Be watchful of others that are present on the highway. Follow the new traffic flow signs and keep vehicle and bicycle speeds at the posted speed limits of 20 mph in general and 10 mph in the S curves. Let’s all stay safe!

title: El Calderon Trail closed for construction through September 2026
description: The El Calderon Trail and parking area are closed from August 11, 2025, through September 19, 2026, for a major improvement project. NPS Road 100 will remain open for local traffic only, and the Continental Divide Trail will remain open for CDT thru-hikers.

title: Juniper Lake Campground Closed
description: The Juniper Lake Campground and day use area is currently closed for maintenance and campground improvement projects. Potable water is not available in the campground. The Juniper Lake Road (access to lake and trailheads) is open. Please drive with caution as road crews and contractors may be actively working along the roadway.

title: Trail Closure
description: A portion of the Headland Trail is closed due to ongoing restoration work. Access to the trail will now close at 2:30 pm daily. All hikers must be off the trails by 4:45 pm.

title: Adjacent public land access remains impacted by Babylon Fire
description: Road access is closed west of Cathedral Butte Trailhead and east of Beef Basin per the Bureau of Land Management order. Backpackers are able to access the trailhead for trips into Salt Creek. Motor vehicle and bicycle traffic can access Beef Basin via Elephant Hill 4WD Road only.

title: Jamaica Bay Wildlife Refuge Visitor Center Phone Out of Order
description: The Jamaica Bay Wildlife Refuge Visitor Center phone line (718-318-4340) is not working at this time. Please monitor social media (Instagram and Facebook) or call our general park information line at 718-354-4606 for program or other park updates. For emergencies, call U.S. Park Police dispatch at 718-354-4700.

title: Authorized drone flight over park for the next several days
description: Vicksburg National Military Park authorized a UAS/drone to operate over the park for the next several days. If you are interested in learning more or have questions, please contact the Special Use Permit Coordinator, John Castaldo at john_castaldo@nps.gov

title: Road work at El Malpais Visitor Center
description: Repaving of the El Malpais Visitor Center parking lot will occur in July. The visitor center will remain open, but slight delays are possible. Please follow construction signage and directions.

title: Temporary Emergency Fire Closure
description: Open fires of any kind, including charcoal fires, are prohibited until conditions improve. Smoking is prohibited except for in vehicles or buildings where indicated. Use of gas stoves is permitted in areas that are clear of flammable materials.

title: Devils Kitchen parking lot closure, no water 8/3-28
description: From August 3rd to 28th, 2026, a contractor will replace the leaky waterline at the Devils Kitchen Picnic Area. The main parking lot at the picnic area will be closed during this time, and water will be shut off throughout most of the project. Port-a-Johns will be located at the trailhead parking across the street, and the overflow parking lot will be open next to the East Entrance.

title: Bathroom closure at Sugar Run Picnic shelter
description: Due to a yellow jacket nest, the bathrooms at Sugar Run Picnic shelter are closed

title: Visitor Center Open at 419 Decatur Street
description: The New Orleans Jazz NHP & Jean Lafitte NHP&P have a combined French Quarter Visitor Center at 419 Decatur Street. Open Tuesdays through Saturdays, 9:30 am to 4:30 pm. Calendar for events: https://www.nps.gov/jazz/planyourvisit/calendar.

title: Closure at Maryland Heights for Peregrines LIFTED 7/23/26
description: The annual closure of certain areas of Maryland Heights for peregrine falcon nesting has been lifted as of 7/23/26. Climbing areas closed for the peregrines are now OPEN.

title: Limited parking at the Train Station 7/27-7/30/26
description: There will be a significant disruption to parking availability and circulation within the Train Station parking lot on July 27-July 30. Portions of the parking lot will be blocked to allow for safe use of equipment needed for geotechnical work. The Train Station will remain open. Additional parking is available at the Visitor Center parking lot, 171 Shoreline Drive, Harpers Ferry.

title: Visitor center bookstore closed August 26 for inventory
description: The Western National Parks (WNP) bookstore at the El Malpais Visitor Center will be closed for annual inventory on Wednesday, August 26, 2026. The rest of the visitor center will be open as usual from 9:00 am to 5:00 pm. You can shop your western national parks online at the link below. Thank you for your understanding!

title: NPS 300 Road Conditions
description: NPS 300 to Big Tubes has not been evaluated since the most recent rainstorms. A high clearance, four-wheel-drive vehicle is recommended.

title: Partial Trail Closure
description: The crossover trail through the center of the historic area, near the flagpole, is temporarily closed for safety. The remainder of the main park trail is open.

title: USS Cassin Young
description: USS CASSIN YOUNG is currently closed due to maintenance work on Pier One in the Charlestown Navy Yard. The ship is tentatively scheduled to re-open to the public the end of August.

title: Harmful Algae Bloom
description: A Harmful Algae Bloom has been confirmed in recent water samples taken from the Nelson's Landing and the Cottonwood Cove areas on Lake Mohave. To reduce health risks, the National Park Service recommends recreators limit body contact with these waters when algae is present. Please click here for pictures of this dangerous cyanobacteria and contact the Park at 702-293-8990 for updates on this advisory.

title: Extreme Heat Warning Through Monday July 27th
description: The National Weather Service has issued an Extreme Heat Warning through at least Monday July 27th for the Las Vegas and Lake Mead area. Visitors should limit outdoor activities on land within the recreation area, drink plenty of water, and be alert for symptoms of heat illness including thirst, heavy sweating, muscle cramps, weakness/dizziness, headache, and nausea. Anyone experiencing these symptoms should move indoors in air conditioning immediately.

title: Central Campground Closure
description: Central Group Campground will be closed from July 27, 2026 - August 6, 2026 for road construction and repairs. Reservations cannot be made during this time. The campground will reopen on August 7.

title: Heat Advisory in Effect
description: The National Weather Service has issued a heat advisory for Northeast Florida from July 22-29th with a heat index value ranging 105-110 degrees F. Please adjust your plans accordingly and ensure you stay hydrated during your visit.

title: Dispersed and Backcountry Fires Prohibited
description: Due to increased fire activity and dry vegetation, dispersed and backcountry fires are prohibited. Fires within established metal fire rings in developed campgrounds and picnic areas are allowed. Propane and gas stoves are allowed, if operated at least three feet away from flammable vegetation and forest litter.

title: Lava Tube Bridge Replacement
description: Most of Nāhuku lava tube trail is open during bridge replacement but is only accessible one way in and out from the east “exit” end. The rainforest trail to the front of the lava tube, the lava tube bridge and 50 feet into the cave are temporarily closed during the replacement. The project should be complete by mid-August. The restrooms are open.

title: Kīpukapuaulu Trail Temporary Closed Due to Hazardous Trees
description: Kīpukapuaulu Trail is temporarily closed due to hazardous trees that require further assessment and potential removal for safety. The park is working on a hazard tree safety plan. The closure could last several more weeks.

title: Steel Creek Water Outage
description: There is a temporary water outage at Steel Creek and water will not be available until further notice. In the meantime, you should bring all the water you’ll need for your visit, including drinking water. Pit toilets will be available for use. Please contact Tyler Bend Visitor Center at 870-439-2502 if you have any questions or would like additional information.

title: Temporary Delays & Closures for Bobcat and Fox Trails July 22 - August 7
description: Roads crew will be working on Bobcat Trail and Fox Trail starting July 22 through August 7. Bobcat will remain open during maintenance, but Fox Trail will be closed starting July 23. Work will be from 8 AM to 4 PM Monday through Friday. Please obey closures and stay away from work sites.

title: Outer Island Nighttime Closure
description: Outer Island is closed to all use from 10 PM to 6 AM due to bear activity and food‑storage concerns. Day use is permitted outside these hours. The closure remains in effect until further notice to protect visitor safety and support ongoing wildlife management.

title: Temporary Closure - July 30th
description: The visitor center, caves, and cave access trail will be closed on July 30th for all employee meetings. The picnic areas and Swinging Bridge Nature Trail remain open.

title: Trail Closure - Dunewood Trace
description: Temporary closure of the Dunewood Trace trail (2.2 miles), between Kemil Rd, and the Dunewood Campground (near the recycle bins), is now in effect until further notice due to construction of the new Marquette Greenway trail.

title: Landslide hazard - Root Glacier Trail Closed Area
description: There is unstable ground at the moraine (rock adjacent to a glacier) that is above the northern end of the Root Glacier Trail. Hikers should not enter this area. If anyone enters the area because they are returning from a backcountry trip on the other side of the glacier, they should not linger.

title: Upper Fort Mason Roads and Parking Area Closures Fall 2025 - Fall 2026
description: Roads and parking areas at upper Fort Mason will have closures during utilities and seismic retrofit projects. Closures planned Fall 2025 through Fall 2026. Lots will be fenced and used as staging areas for projects occurring at Fort Mason. Signs will be posted in advance of utilities work as project progresses through each area at Fort Mason. Read signs and do not park in posted areas. Vehicles will be towed at owner's expense.

title: Schonchin Butte Closure
description: Schonchin Butte Road and Trail are closed to all traffic when the gate is closed, due to maintenance work occurring at the fire lookout.

title: 8/3/26 - 8/28/26 Closure at Devils Kitchen Picnic Area Parking Lot
description: From 8/3/26 to 8/28/26, contractors will be repairing and replacing the waterline at Devils Kitchen Picnic Area and parking lot. The restrooms, water, and parking area will be closed throughout the duration of the project. Access to Serpents Trail will remain open at the Devils Kitchen Trailhead.

title: No Lifeguards at Race Point Beach
description: There are no lifeguards on duty at Race Point Beach. Swim at your own risk.

title: No Lifeguards at Herring Cove Beach
description: There are no lifeguards on duty at Herring Cove Beach. Swim at your own risk.

title: Construction for Seawall Project
description: Starting July 27, 2026, Castillo de San Marcos National Monument will begin construction to replace, raise and rehabilitate the park’s failing seawalls. The historic fort will remain accessible throughout the project. Some areas outside of the fort will be closed for safety.

title: Lower Sand Creek CLOSED from Crossing with Music Pass and Sand Ramp Trails
description: The following locations shall be closed to public entry: 20 yards on both sides or shorelines of Sand Creek from the junction of the creek and the Music Pass Trail, downstream to where the Music Pass Trail connects to the Sand Ramp Trai from 12:00 a.m. on July 26th, 2026 and remain in effect until 11:59 p.m. on August 2nd, 2026. CAUTION! Water in Sand Creek will not be potable for drinking, pets, or livestock during this closure. Trail access on nearby trails remains OPEN.

title: LBJ Ranch Reopened Sunday, July 19.
description: Following the flooding which took place July 16, the LBJ Ranch reopened for normal operational hours (9am to 5pm) on Sunday, July 19. The ranch driving route is fully open, and visitors will be able to enter the Junction School and Showbarn as well as view the cemetery and walk to the Reconstructed Birthplace. The sites in the Johnson City District of the park remain open; this includes the national park visitor center and Boyhood Home.

title: Stockton Island Trail Access
description: The trail between Presque Isle Bay and Quarry Bay on Stockton Island is open, but a footbridge on the western portion of the trail was washed out in a 2024 storm. Visitors must wade through shallow water or take an alternate route.

title: Ongoing Closure Notices
description: Devils Island dock and campsites and West Bay Club on Sand Island are closed. These closures affect only a small portion of the Lakeshore. Enjoy your visit.

title: Current East Rim Trail Status: Open
description: As of Thursday, July 16, 2026, the East Rim Trail System remains open. For more information, visit the website linked below. In good conditions the mountain bike trails are open 6 am-11 pm for bikers and as posted for other trail users. In wet or hazardous conditions, the trail will close to all users to prevent damage. Be flexible; conditions may change throughout the day.

title: Painted Hills Unit Closed due to the Rowe Creek Complex Fires
description: Due to threats from the Rowe Creek Complex which started on July 15 and is currently estimated at approximately 142,936 acres, the Wheeler County Sheriff’s Office has issued a Level 3/Go, Evacuation order for the zone that includes much of the Painted Hills Unit of John Day Fossil Beds National Monument. An Emergency Closure of the Painted Hills Unit has been implemented to protect public safety. The Unit Painted Hills Unit is closed to all entry as of 1530 hours on July 17, 2026.

title: Elevator in Statue's Lobby Temporarily Out of Service
description: The Statue of Liberty lobby elevator is currently out of service. Visitors will need to climb the stairs to the mezzanine level to access the main pedestal elevator.

title: Culvert Replacement at Netul Landing
description: From July 27–August 12, 2026, we’re replacing a failing culvert to improve road safety and enhance fish habitat connectivity at Lewis and Clark NHP. For Netul Trail access, please park at the North Netul bus shelter. Parking remains open for kayak launch and picnic shelters at South Netul. Thank you for your patience as we work to protect both visitors and our environment!

title: Road Work Along FR 545 at Sunset Crater
description: Road work will occur along FR 545 at Sunset Crater on Wednesday, July 22, and potentially Thursday, July 23. Work will take place at the base of Sunset Crater, just past the Lava Flow Parking Area. During this project, traffic will be limited to one lane. Drivers should expect periodic full traffic stoppages in both directions. Please plan for minor delays and use caution when traveling through the area.

title: Road Work Along FR 545 at Sunset Crater
description: Road work will occur along FR 545 at Sunset Crater on Wednesday, July 22, and potentially Thursday, July 23. Work will take place at the base of Sunset Crater, just past the Lava Flow Parking Area. During this project, traffic will be limited to one lane. Drivers should expect periodic full traffic stoppages in both directions. Please plan for minor delays and use caution when traveling through the area.

title: Smokey air from local wildfires
description: Current air quality is being influenced by local fires and can change in an instant. Check https://www.airnow.gov/? for specific air quality index (AQI) information for your favorite spot at Lake Roosevelt National Recreation Area.

title: Clarno Unit Closed due to Rowe Creek Complex Fires
description: Due to threats from the Rowe Creek Complex fires that started on July 15 and has burned onto the eastern edge of Clarno Unit. An Emergency Closure of the Clarno Unit has been implemented to protect public safety. The Clarno Unit is closed to all entry as of 0100 hours on July 17, 2026.

title: Home of FDR - Partial Closure of Rose Garden
description: The planting beds, lawns, and paths of the Rose Garden will be under construction from late March 2026 lasting through fall of 2026. This rehabilitation will restore the crisp, level character of the garden, improve access and infrastructure, and re-install historic rose and peony varieties. During this period, the Burial Site viewing area should remain available, but occasional disruptions may restrict public access. The graves, marble monument, pet graves, and sundial will not be impacted by this project.

title: Campfire ban and fire restrictions in effect parkwide
description: Due to high fire danger and active wildfires across northeast Minnesota, Voyageurs National Park will implement increased fire restrictions. The restrictions will remain in effect until rescinded. Under this restriction, the ignition, building, maintaining, attending, or use of campfires is prohibited within the park. This includes charcoal grills, barbecues, and any fires fueled by wood or charcoal. These restrictions align with broader state and regional restrictions.

title: Manzanar Remains Open During US 395 Pavement Project
description: CalTrans begins a monthslong pavement project on US 395 adjacent to Manzanar National Historic Site on Monday, May 11, 2026. Crews will be working to ensure access to Manzanar remains open, but it will be important to travel cautiously as typical access may involve detours and map apps may be inaccurate. Though work is scheduled only during weekdays, lane closures and detours will be in place throughout the week. Currently, the site may only be accessed via the south entrance.

title: Visiting During Monsoon Season (July-September)
description: All park trails are closed for 30 minutes following any lightning strikes five miles or less from the park. This includes Montezuma Well and the trail to see Montezuma Castle. Please check the forecast ahead of your visit.

title: Visiting During Monsoon Season (July-September)
description: All park trails are closed for 30 minutes following any lightning strikes five miles or less from the park. This includes the Pueblo Trail and Tavasci Marsh Trail. Please check the forecast ahead of your visit.

title: Visitor Center Contact Phone Down
description: The Theodore Roosevelt Birthplace contact phone, (212) 260-1616, is currently experiencing issues. Rangers may not be able to receive your call. For questions, please email thrb_info@nps.gov.

title: Road Construction
description: There will be road construction at both park units starting June 29, 2026, to approximately July 31, 2026. Temporary traffic controls will be in place, and flaggers will guide visitors. Please follow all posted traffic control devices and directions from construction personnel. Construction schedules may be adjusted due to weather or operational needs.

title: Phone Lines Down
description: All phone line are currently down at Longfellow House-Washington's Headquarters National Historic Site. While we work to fix this, please contact us via email for any inquiries or requests: long_info@nps.gov.

title: East Portal Road
description: Until further notice, East Portal Road and campground are closed due to flood damage.

title: East Portal Road
description: Until further notice, East Portal Road and campground are closed due to flood damage.

title: Temporary Phone Number — (575) 243-2914
description: We are currently experiencing an extended phone service outage affecting our main park phone lines. If you have questions or need assistance, please call (575) 243-2914 to speak with a staff member. This temporary phone line is available daily between 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. (Mountain Time). If we are helping another visitor, please leave a message and we will get back to you as soon as we can. We apologize for the inconvenience and appreciate your patience as we work to restore normal phone service.

title: Poor Air Quality
description: Due to wildfires in the region around the park visitors should expect varying levels of poor air quality due to smoke. For current air quality check the fire and smoke map here: https://fire.airnow.gov/

title: No Water Available at Ok-A-Beh Marina - Flushing Restrooms Closed
description: Due to a water shortage, flushable toilets are currently unavailable at the Ok-A-Beh Marina. Vault toilets are available at the upper parking lot and a floating restroom is available on the courtesy dock.

title: Construction at Blow-Me-Down Mill
description: The area around the Blow-Me-Down Mill and Dam are temporarily closed through August due to work to repair and reinforce the foundation of the Blow-Me-Down Mill.

title: Bear Gulch Cave Closed
description: Due to maternal bat colonies present in Bear Gulch Cave, and in line with the expected seasonal closure scheduling, the Bear Gulch Caves are currently closed. The Balconies Cave remains open, and accessible from the Balconies or Old Pinnacles trails.

title: Lindenwald Reopens For Tours
description: Martin Van Buren National Historic Site will reopen Lindenwald for guided tours beginning Friday, July 17, 2026. While the mansion will be open, access to portions of the historic grounds remains limited as park staff continue cleanup and recovery efforts. Visitors are asked to respect all posted closures and stay out of restricted areas for their safety. Thank you for your patience and understanding as we continue this important work.

title: Construction Activity at Little Sand Bay; Boat and Kayak Access Maintained
description: Construction for the Little Sand Bay Marina Rehabilitation Project begins May 1. The Town of Russell boat launch and the NPS kayak beach will remain open, with short detours around work areas. Expect reduced parking, delays, and increased noise. The Little Sand Bay Visitor Center will be closed in 2026 due to construction.

title: Sculptor's Studio Heat Advisory
description: The Sculptor’s Studio may close temporarily during periods of high heat to protect visitors and staff. Please check with park staff upon arrival for the most up‑to‑date information on whether the Studio is open or closed.

title: Avoid Water Contact at Sand Beach Lagoon (Not for Sand Beach)
description: Bacterial levels have exceeded public health standards at Sand Beach Lagoon and a Public Health Advisory has been posted. The public is advised against swimming at this beach until bacterial levels return to healthful levels. (Not for Sand Beach.)

title: Bighorn Lake Elevation is Below 3625ft
description: When lake levels are below 3625, boaters are advised to avoid areas south of Horseshoe Bend and the South Narrows due to low water levels. Throughout the year, lake water levels fluctuate greatly. Hazards and launching abilities change with the water levels. Please use caution when recreating on Bighorn Lake.

title: Sections of moat wall closed until Winter 2026
description: Sections of the moat wall that were damaged by Hurricanes Helene and Milton (2024) are undergoing repair and reinforcement. For your safety, please follow posted signage and do not cross any barricades.

title: Fire Danger VERY HIGH
description: Wood-burning fires and charcoal grills are prohibited. Propane and gas stoves allowed only in campground and picnic areas for cooking food. No smoking on trail. No roadside parking. Fireworks are always prohibited.

title: Current Alerts and Conditions
description: Be sure to review the Alerts and Conditions below before and during your visit for additional, up-to-date information on closures, cautions, and other current park conditions.

title: Solstice Canyon Trail Weekday Closure for Repairs
description: Solstice Canyon Trail will be closed Monday through Thursday starting July 13, 2026, while crews complete repair work. During closure hours, visitors must enter and exit via Rising Sun Trail. All trails remain open on weekends (including Fridays). The project is expected to last approximately four weeks.

title: Accessible Parking Available
description: Accessible parking is available at the George Washington Carver Museum and The Oaks. For George Washington Carver Museum, after receiving your visitor pass, enter Tuskegee University through Lincoln Gates on Booker T. Washington Boulevard. Pass Margaret Murray Washington Hall and the Kellogg Hotel and Conference Center, then turn right to the parking garage. Accessible parking for The Oaks is at 1200 West Montgomery Road. For assistance, call Sheryl Buchanan at (334) 421-3246

title: Phones Down at the Tuskegee Airmen National Historic Site
description: For any general inquiries and reservations, visitors can contact Ranger Tommy Smith at (334) 421-0340.

title: Status of Cascading Fountain at Meridian Hill Park
description: We appreciate your patience as we work to remove the sediment from the Meridian Hill Cascading Fountain. The discoloration occurred when two long-unused water lines were brought back online as part of our continuing effort to fine-tune the fountain’s operations. Visitors should begin seeing the fountain’s signature sparkling water again soon.

title: No cold-water flow at the Serpentine Hot Springs bathhouse
description: There is currently no cold-water flow into the tub at Serpentine Hot Springs. Please proceed with caution. The National Park Service plans to complete repairs on the cold‑water pipe in August. Visitors are respectfully advised not to dig ditches or otherwise attempt to establish alternative cold‑water access. Thank you for your cooperation.

title: Detour along Mount Vernon Trail at Gravelly Point
description: Due to constriction for the Long Bridge Project, the Mount Vernon Trail will be temporarily detoured around the construction zone beginning on July 15, 2026. Trail users should expect periodic crossings of equipment and materials where the trail meets the construction access road. Detour will be in place through 2030.

title: Areas of Meridian Hill Park closed for turf restoration
description: The turf at Meridian Hill Park is closed through August 17 while we make the park safer and more enjoyable for everyone. Thank you for your patience.

title: Duncan Narrows Campground Closed
description: Duncan Narrows Campground is closed, including Duncan Narrows tent site, shelters, and dock. Day use of the campground is also closed. This closure is necessary due to the increasing frequency of wolf-human interactions, and continued non-compliance with food storage regulations. Closed areas will be patrolled to ensure compliance.

title: For Visitor information or assistance, Call (334) 727-3200
description: For visitor information or assistance at Tuskegee Institute National Historic Site, please call (334) 727-3200.For group reservations please call Sheryl Buchanan at (334) 421-3246.

title: Wind Cave Canyon Trail Closed for Repair and Improvement
description: Wind Cave Canyon Trail is closed so that the trail and adjoining road can be repaired from frequent washouts. Sixteen low water crossings will be hardened and the road resurfaced. The trail could be closed for several weeks. This closure does not affect any cave tours.

title: Fire Operations
description: Wildfires are occurring in the region. Water scooping airplanes are using the reservoir. Please use caution and stay clear of areas where water scooping operations are occurring.

title: Do not pick up hitchhikers
description: Do not pick up hitchhikers. Please report their locations to law enforcement by calling 911.

title: Church & under trees in high wind conditions
description: Avoid area around the church & under trees in high wind conditions

title: Sidewalk scaffolding at Federal Hall
description: Protective sidewalk scaffolding has been erected around the building as a safety precaution.

title: Phone lines working intermittently
description: Our phone lines are working intermittently. If you are not able to reach us by phone, please email us at bela_information@nps.gov.

title: Roadway Work to Begin at Sanford Yake Campgournd Monday, July 13th
description: The National Park Service announces that Federal Highway Administration contractors will begin roadway and pavement maintenance at Sanford Yake Campground starting Monday, July 13, 2026. This project will include chip seal, micro seal, micro surfacing, and pavement striping throughout key areas of Lake Meredith National Recreation Area. Visitors to Alibates Flint Quarries National Monument and Lake Meredith National Recreation Area are encouraged to follow all posted message boards and traffic instructions.

title: Roadwork to Begin at Sanford Yake Campground Monday, July 13th
description: The National Park Service announces that Federal Highway Administration contractors will begin roadway and pavement maintenance at Sanford Yake Campground starting Monday, July 13, 2026. This project will include chip seal, micro seal, micro surfacing, and pavement striping throughout key areas of Lake Meredith National Recreation Area. Visitors to Alibates Flint Quarries National Monument and Lake Meredith National Recreation Area are encouraged to follow all posted message boards and traffic instructions.

title: Paving Work Ongoing Throughout the Park
description: Paving work is being done throughout Ozark National Scenic Riverways during the 2026 summer season, including at Alley Spring, Round Spring, Pulltite, and Big Spring. Watch here and on our park Facebook page for updates, as roads and campground loops may close and reopen depending on work progress.

title: Round Spring Pavilion Parking Area Closed
description: The parking lot for the Round Spring Pavilion and for Round Spring itself is CLOSED for the remainder of the 2026 summer season while the low water bridge over Spring Valley Creek is rebuilt. Alternative parking near Round Spring Group Campsites 4-8 will provide trail access to the north side of Round Spring.

title: Round Spring Lower River Landing Closed
description: The lower river landing at Round Spring, located in the campground, is closed until further notice for paving. Floaters putting in or taking out at Round Spring should plan to use the upper landing behind Carr's Store.

title: Accessible Lift Inoperable at Parsonage
description: The accessible wheelchair lift for the Parsonage building is undergoing maintenance as of 7/10/26. Visitors who are unable to use stairs may not be able to enter the parsonage until this issue is resolved.

title: Avoid Ticks on Site!
description: Ticks are very active at New Philadelphia. Use insect repellant and stay on trails. Avoid brushing against logs, shrubs, and grasses. Check your body for ticks after your visit. Learn more about keeping safe from ticks on the Safety page.

title: Total Fire Restrictions Implemented June 20, 2026
description: Due to extreme fire conditions, all fires at Lake Roosevelt National Recreation Area are prohibited effective 12:01 a.m., June 20, until further notice. No open flames are permitted. Only self-contained propane or gas cookstoves and lanterns are allowed during the full fire ban.

title: Tent Camping Closed at Three Mile Campground
description: Due to increased human-wildlife interactions and food storage concerns, individual tent sites and group sites at Three Mile Campground are currently closed. Tent and hammock camping are not permitted anywhere within the campground. Off-trail camping zones 11, 12, and 33 are closed. Shelters remain open. Food, trash, and scented items must be stored in animal-resistant, hard-sided containers or food storage lockers. Backpacks must be stored in shelters. Closed areas will be patrolled to ensure compliance.

title: Traffic Delays - Gibbon River Bridge
description: Expect up to 15-minute delays on Gibbon River Bridge from July 9 through late-July while crews repair the railing.

title: Schoolhouse and the Schoolhouse Spur Trail Closed for Maintenance
description: Beginning July 14, 2026 the Lower Fox Creek school and the surrounding area (including parking lot) will be closed to receive a new roof. Schoolhouse Spur Trail and the creek crossing on the Southwind Nature Trail will be closed to accommodate this construction zone. The schoolhouse area, including the access road leading to the school, will be closed through approximately August 8, 2026. For your safety, please do not venture beyond closure signs.

title: Cross Plains Segment — Partial Trail Closure
description: The western 0.3 miles of the Cross Plains Segment, from Sherwood Forest Lane to Park Street, is closed. When hiking eastbound, continue southwest on CTH‑KP, then head east on USH‑14 and turn north on Market Street. This 0.8‑mile bypass replaces 0.5 miles of connecting route and Ice Age Trail. Stay alert. Use caution. Keep dogs leashed.

title: Stehekin is Open, Services Limited at Stehekin Landing
description: Visitor and recreational opportunities continue to be available in the Stehekin Valley. Some services are limited at the Stehekin Landing following flood damage in December 2025.

title: Mora Road Closed for Essential Repairs
description: Mora Road is closed to all traffic, including bicycles and pedestrians, at the campground. Rialto Beach is not accessible via Mora Road during this construction period. Mora Campground is open. This construction work will repair damage from a severe winter flood event, fortify the road against river migration, and protect long-term access to Rialto Beach.

title: Fort Jay front gate only — Temporary Closure.
description: The FRONT GATE of Fort Jay is temporarily closed to all. The fort is currently open to visitation Wednesday thru Sunday 10am to 4pm. Access to the fort will be via the western or rear sallyport.

title: Stage II Fire Restrictions
description: Fire danger is extremely high. No fires (charcoal or wood) are permitted anywhere in the park, including in the campground. No smoking outside of your vehicle. Fireworks are always banned. Check vehicles for dragging chains. Be safe and fire aware!

title: Staircase Developed Area is Open, Use Caution in Burned Areas
description: The Staircase developed area is open. The surrounding wilderness areas will remain closed as repair and recovery efforts continue. Use extreme caution when entering burned areas. Burned landscapes may contain falling trees and branches, loose boulders, unstable ground, stump holes, landslides, and debris flows. Changing conditions such as wind, rain, or storms can rapidly trigger hazards. Learn more on our Fire Conditions and Updates page.

title: Kennesaw Mountain Dr. Closed to Private Vehicles and Cyclists
description: Starting January 5th, 2026, the road to the top of Kennesaw Mountain will be closed to private vehicles and cyclists due to construction and painting. Shuttle service to the top of the mountain is ONLY available on weekends and select federal holidays. The park's Visitor Center is still accessible. This work is in preparation for the upcoming Safety Improvement Project. For updates, continue to check park's website.

title: Partial Closures to Little Calumet River Trail and Glenwood Dunes Trail
description: Marquette Greenway construction will require closing sections of the Glenwood Dunes Trail (April–December 2026) and Little Calumet River / Mnoké Prairie Trail (May–December 2026). Closure dates may shift as work progresses. Please follow all posted closures and check the park website or NPS App for updates.

title: Great Sand Dunes At Stage 2 Fire Restrictions - No Open Fires.
description: As of 12pm on June 29th Great Sand Dunes officially entered stage 2 fire restrictions due to ongoing dry, warm, and windy conditions. During stage 2 fire restrictions the following requirements are in effect: Prohibited: Open flame including fire, campfire, stove fire, charcoal grills and barbeques, coal and wood burning stoves. Smoking outside of an enclosed personal vehicle or trailer. Permitted: Devices using pressurized gas canisters for isobutene or propane that include shut-off valves.

title: Fire Response Impacts on Lake Powell
description: Until further notice, boaters are advised that aircraft may be operating at low altitude and making repeated passes to collect water as part of ongoing response efforts to the Babylon Fire. Fire suppression aircraft will be scooping water from Lake Powell between Good Hope Bay and Castle Butte. Mariners should exercise heightened caution, remain alert for aviation activity, and reduce speed when boating through the area. Boaters need to monitor marine radio channel 16.

title: Hobart Woodland Trail Temporary Closure
description: Hobart Woodland is closed until further notice while park crews work to clear several downed trees that are creating hazardous conditions for visitors.

title: Munising Falls Trail Closed Until Further Notice
description: The Munising Falls Trail within Pictured Rocks National Lakeshore is closed until further notice. Approximately 75-feet of the paved trail was washed out April 28th from recent heavy rainfall and seasonal snow melt.

title: Beach Closure in Place in Front of Buxton Village
description: The entire beachfront in front of Buxton Village is temporarily closed to public entry due to the presence of threatened oceanfront structures.

title: Church Loop Trail Closure
description: The Church Loop Trail in the Thurmond area of the park is temporarily closed due to downed trees.

title: Stage 2 fire restrictions in effect
description: No setting, building, maintaining, attending, or using open fires of any kind in the park. This includes campfires and charcoal fires in Watchman Campground, South Campground, and picnic areas in Zion Canyon. Stoves fueled by petroleum or liquid propane gas are allowed. Smoking is prohibited, except within an enclosed vehicle.

title: Stage II Fire Restrictions in effect - campfires banned
description: Stage II Fire Restrictions are in effect at Great Basin National Park. Due to extreme fire danger, campfires, charcoal grills, and outdoor smoking are prohibited throughout the park. Gas and liquid-fueled stoves are permitted.

title: Yosemite Traffic Updates
description: When the park is very busy, you can get updates on current traffic conditions in Yosemite by texting ynptraffic to 333111.

title: Guided Tours Available by Appointment Only
description: To request a guided tour, please contact the park a minimum of two weeks in advance. The grounds and outbuildings of Oakland Plantation and Magnolia Plantation are open for self-guided tours from 9:00 am to 3:30 pm Wednesday through Sunday.

title: Food Storage Regulations in Effect
description: Proper food storage is required on Isle Royale. All food, trash, scented items, cooking supplies, cooking utensils, and fish/fish parts must be stored properly. To learn more about food storage and to learn how to properly store your food, trash, and scented items, click "more."

description: The parking lot, boardwalk, and Firehole River at Biscuit Basin, located north of Old Faithful, is closed to all travel until further notice due to the possibility of another event at the site of a hydrothermal explosion that occurred July 23, 2024.

description: Due to HVAC system issues, Arlington House may close to visitors when interior temperatures reach 85°F. Temporary closures may occur with little notice to protect the safety and comfort of visitors and staff.

description: East Rim Drive is currently CLOSED to all public access from Park Headquarters to Phantom Ship Overlook for road construction. West Rim Drive, North Entrance Road, East Rim Drive from North Junction to Phantom Ship Overlook, Cloudcap Road, and Pinnacles Road are now OPEN for travel.

title: IA 76 in both directions: Road construction
description: IA 76 in both directions: Road construction affecting traffic to Effigy Mounds National Monument. Expect short delays.

title: Mainland Museum Closure
description: The Cumberland Island Museum will be closed for an extended period due to roof leakages. We apologize for any inconvenience but look forward to reopening to you in the future.

title: Stage II Fire Restrictions
description: Stage II fire restrictions are in effect until further notice. Campfires including charcoal are not permitted, even in established fire rings. Smoking is only permitted within an enclosed vehicle. Gas or liquid fueled portable camp stoves are still permitted.

title: 6/30/26 - 8/7/26 Devils Kitchen Picnic Area - Expect Temporary Closures
description: June 30 through August 7, from 6:00 am - 4:30 pm, Monday through Thursday, mason workers will be repointing Devils Kitchen Picnic Shelter to improve the integrity and stability of the structure. The restrooms will remain open, but the picnic tables may be inaccessible during construction.

title: Cave Tour Reservations
description: Advance cave tour reservations up until August 31st are available. September reservations will become available on August 1st. Reservations are strongly recommended. Reservations full? Choose a day to come to the park early in the day to purchase a same day cave tour ticket.

title: Partial Trail Closure at Portage Lakefront and Riverwalk
description: Closed portion of Portage Lakefront and Riverwalk Trail along Burns Waterway due to unsafe conditions from erosional damage. This trail portion will remain closed while funding is sought for repair work. Pier access remains open on either side of closure.

title: Public Health Advisory for Upper Clear Creek above Whiskeytown Lake
description: ***Please Note: there is no increased risk to swimming in Whiskeytown Lake currently. This public health advisory is specific to Upper Clear Creek.*** Recent water quality monitoring in Clear Creek in and around Tower House Historic District and Clear Creek Picnic Area has unfortunately detected elevated levels of E. coli bacteria, posing an increased risk to recreational users. Because of this, the National Park Service advises visitors to avoid contact with the water in these areas of the park.

title: Wood & Charcoal Burn Ban
description: To protect park infrastructure and visitors during this hot, dry period of year, wood and charcoal/briquette burning is temporarily banned. Propane grills are still okay. Thank you for recreating responsibly in your national recreation area.

title: Stage 2 Fire Restrictions in Effect
description: Until further notice, the following are PROHIBITED in all park areas: (1) Building, maintaining, attending, or using a fire or campfire, including charcoal fires or pellet grills, or any other open burning. Properly shielded, self-contained propane or liquid-fueled camp stoves and grills, lanterns, or other heated devices with on/off switches are permitted. (2) All smoking, except within a personally-owned enclosed vehicle. (3) Discharging or using any kind of fireworks or other pyrotechnic devices.

title: Stage 2 Fire Restrictions in Effect
description: Until further notice, the following are PROHIBITED in all park areas: (1) Building, maintaining, attending, or using a fire or campfire, including charcoal fires or pellet grills, or any other open burning. Properly shielded, self-contained propane or liquid-fueled camp stoves and grills, lanterns, or other heated devices with on/off switches are permitted. (2) All smoking, except within a personally-owned enclosed vehicle. (3) Discharging or using any kind of fireworks or other pyrotechnic devices.

title: Parts of Santa Rosa Island Closed During Wildfire Recovery
description: Santa Rosa Island reopens to limited day use on July 1. No overnight visits are allowed. Burned areas, including Water Canyon Campground, remain closed through at least August 13. Click the more link for additional information.

title: A Fire Ban (Stage 2 Fire Restrictions) Are In Effect
description: Due to very high fire danger, the extended weather forecast, and current fire activity in the State of Colorado, Stage 2 Fire Restrictions are now in effect within Rocky Mountain National Park. When Stage 2 Fire Restrictions are in effect, this means that all campfires, including charcoal briquette fires are not permitted anywhere within Rocky Mountain National Park. This ban is effective beginning today, June 29, and will remain in effect until further notice.

title: Update on Transponders
description: Due to some unexpected technical issues that are impacting recent transponder sales and renewals, Rocky Mountain National Park is temporarily pausing the sale and renewal of transponder devices. Updates will be posted on the park webpage.

title: Be cautious around park rivers & learn how to cross safely!
description: Many hikers underestimate the power of moving water. Regardless of your knowledge, skills, and experience use these pointers in making wise decisions before attempting to cross a river.

title: Elevated E. Coli levels - Fremont River
description: Recent water quality testing shows elevated E. coli levels in the Fremont River. Use caution if entering the water. Do not get water in your mouth, do not swim. Wash hands with soap and water.

title: Tyler Bend Pavilion Closure
description: Starting on January 20, 2026, the Tyler Bend Pavilion will be closed for construction on the pavilion restrooms. The Tyler Bend Pavilion parking area and Lower Launch River access remain open to the public. The Pavilion is expected to re-open no later than July 11, 2026.

title: Temporary Closure of Park Areas at the Request of US Secret Service
description: At the request of the United States Secret Service and to ensure necessary security and safety for the adjacent White House complex and its occupants, several designated areas of President's Park will be temporarily closed from approximately 12:00 a.m. on Sunday, June 28, 2026, until approximately 11:59 p.m. on Friday, July 31, 2026. For a closure map and more detailed information, please follow the link below.

title: Lees Ferry Campground Partial Closure
description: The upper loop of the Lees Ferry Campground is closed through September 30th for renovations. Large equipment will be paving at the Lees Ferry campground. Upper loop construction will continue until September 30, 2026. Do not enter construction area.

title: Campfires, charcoal fires, or other open fires are not allowed
description: As of Friday June 26, Bryce Canyon is in Stage 2 Fire Restrictions. No setting, building, maintaining, attending, or using of open fires of any kind in the park. This includes campfires and charcoal fires in park campgrounds. Stoves fueled by petroleum or liquid propane gas are allowed. Smoking is not permitted, except inside an enclosed vehicle. Fireworks are never permitted at Bryce Canyon National Park.

title: Current Alerts and Conditions
description: Be sure to review the Alerts and Conditions below before and during your visit for additional, up-to-date information on closures, cautions, and other current park conditions.

title: No Wood or Charcoal Fires Allowed - Stage 2 Fire Restrictions in Effect
description: All fires are prohibited. Only petroleum or propane-fueled stoves or grills are allowed in backcountry campsites, campgrounds, and picnic areas. Fireworks are never allowed. Smoke only inside vehicles or in developed areas over 3 feet from flammables.

title: Phone Number not Working
description: The phone at the park (435-692-1234) is not functioning reliably. People are advised to call 435-241-3951 during business hours in order to speak with a ranger.

title: Park Headquarters Road is closed
description: Park Headquarters Road is closed due to rehabilitation work on the Sugarlands water and wastewater systems.

title: Notice of Stage II Fire Restriction Order in Effect
description: No building, maintaining, attending or using a fire or campfire in all areas of the monument, including charcoal fires. Properly shielded gas or liquid-fueled portable camp stoves are allowed. Smoking is prohibited, except within an enclosed vehicle. Discharging or using fireworks or other pyrotechnic devices are always prohibited on all federal public land.

title: No Wood or Charcoal Fires Allowed - Stage 2 Fire Restrictions in Effect
description: Due to the extremely dry conditions and high fire danger all fires are prohibited. Only petroleum or propane-fueled stoves or grills are allowed in backcountry/river campsites, campgrounds, and picnic areas. Fireworks are never allowed. Smoke only inside vehicles.

title: Annual/Seasonal Canyoneering Closures
description: The following are closed to entry through 8/31/2026 to protect sensitive resources: the heads of Fivemile Wash & Burro Wash descending east 2 miles; Shinob Canyon + all routes descending into Shinob (including Na-gah, Nighthawk, & Timpie); and Arch Nemesis Canyon, including the route exiting at Capitol Gorge + all direct tributary canyons.

title: Fire restrictions: Stage II
description: Starting at 8:00 am on 6/26/2026, Valles Caldera and the Pueblo Parks Group is entering Stage II fire restrictions to reduce fire risk and prevent wildfires.

title: Two Medicine North Shore Trailhead Reroute
description: In 2026, Two Medicine's North Shore Trailhead is not accessible due to construction in the Two Medicine Campground. A reroute has been established to access the North Shore Trail but does require a ford (unbridged water crossing). Directional signage is in place marking the reroute. Hikers may also access Twin Falls, Upper Two Medicine Lake, No Name Lake, and Dawson Pass without a ford, by using the South Shore Trail. Note: this adds approximately 1 mile of distance, one-way.

title: No Wood or Charcoal Fires Allowed - Stage 2 Fire Restrictions in Effect
description: All fires are prohibited. Only petroleum or propane-fueled stoves or grills are allowed in backcountry campsites, campgrounds, and picnic areas. Fireworks are never allowed. Smoke only inside vehicles or in developed areas over 3 feet from flammables.

title: Critical Backcountry Updates/Closures
description: Visit this link for the inner canyon weather forecast, current trail closures, today's heat risk, and drinking water availability.

title: What's Closed and What's Open: South Rim & North Rim
description: Visit this link for a list of the available visitor services in Grand Canyon Village, Desert View, and the North Rim.

title: Parkwide Fire Ban in effect until further notice beginning June 26
description: Beginning Friday 6/26/26 until rescinded, a parkwide fire ban is implemented for all campfires & the ignition of wood, briquettes, or any fuel in fire pits, fire pans, & BBQ grills.

title: Big South Fork’s Brewster Bridge Road to Temporarily Close for Repair
description: Brewster Bridge Road in Big South Fork NRRA will temporarily close for repair and re-pavement beginning on Monday, June 29. The road was heavily damaged from significant rain events in 2022 and 2023. The area boat launch and day use area will be inaccessible during the project.

title: Stage 2 Fire Restrictions
description: Stage 2 Fire Restrictions in effect as of June 28, 2026. Prohibited actions: all open fires, including charcoal; smoking within 3 feet of vegetation; grinding, cutting, welding, or similar work; operating internal‑combustion engines without spark arrestors; use of flares, exploding targets, incendiary devices; firearm discharge except for during a lawful hunt. Allowed: portable stoves with gas, jellied petroleum, or pressurized liquid fuel, with shut‑off valve used 3 feet or more from any vegetation.

title: Campfire Ban in All Portions of the Park Complex Begins June 29
description: Effective Monday, June 29, campfires or the ignition of wood, briquettes, or any fuel in fire pits, fire pans, and barbeque grills, are banned in all portions of North Cascades National Park Service Complex, which includes North Cascades National Park, Ross Lake National Recreation Area, and Lake Chelan National Recreation Area.. This applies to anything that produces ash, including charcoal grills. Propane fire pits are not allowed during the ban.

title: Fort Union National Monument Under Stage II Fire Restrictions
description: Fort Union National Monument has implemented Stage II fire restrictions effective Wednesday, June 25, 2026. Under Stage II restrictions smoking is prohibited, except in enclosed vehicles or buildings. These restrictions are necessary to help reduce fire risk and prevent wildfires.

title: East Trail System Parking Area Closed.
description: The East Trail System parking area is closed due to storm damage. (Updated 6/24/26)

title: Patriots Point Ferries Accessibility Information
description: Ferries to Fort Sumter from Patriots Point are not always accessible for individuals who use mobility assistance devices or have trouble navigating stairs. The Fort Sumter Visitor Center departure location is fully accessible or visitors can call Fort Sumter Tours (843-722-2628) for current Patriots Point accessibility conditions.

title: Stage II Fire Restrictions
description: Stage II Fire Restrictions are currently in effect due to high fire danger. Restrictions include no campfires and no smoking except in an enclosed vehicle or other authorized area.

title: Going-to-the-Sun Road is Open for 2026 Season
description: The Going-to-the-Sun Road is fully open for the 2026 summer season. The road may now be accessed by motorized vehicles over Logan Pass from both the West Glacier and St. Mary Entrances.

title: Areas of Meridian Hill Park closed for repairs
description: Much of the upper level of the park is closed to rehabilitate the grass. Fountains and the reflecting pool are open but may be turned off or drained occasionally for maintenance. The reflecting pool will undergo repairs June 20-28. Visit the Meridian Hill Park page for more information.

title: Hazardous Hiking Conditions on Lassen Peak Trail
description: Use caution hiking over snow-covered sections on the Lassen Peak trail. Hikers are encouraged to use trekking poles and wear deep-tread hiking boots. Wearing boot spikes will add additional stability over snow-covered sections.

title: Current Park Closures
description: Closures may occur due to inclement weather, construction projects, or other emergency conditions. Please visit the linked page for information about current closures.

title: Please use caution when visiting park grounds.
description: Park grounds and walking paths are accessible but visitors should use caution as there are fallen trees, stumps, and other typhoon debris.

title: Death Canyon Trailhead Construction Closure
description: Death Canyon Road and Trailhead are closed to all use. Start hikes at alternative trailheads such as Granite Canyon, LSR Preserve, and Taggart Lake.

title: Limited access to areas at Asan Beach.
description: Due to the impacts of Typhoon Sinlaku, areas of Asan Beach remain inaccessible. Visitors should use caution when walking to the beach area and stay out of damaged areas.

title: Talisman-Barrett Beach Dock Closed for 2026 Season; Services Limited
description: Due to damage from winter ice, the Talisman-Barrett Beach dock is closed. NPS staff are evaluating options for repairs. There is no timeline for restoration. Boaters should plan to anchor in the bay to access the site. Be advised that the area is extremely shallow. Restroom maintenance will be limited during this time and visitors must pack out all trash and belongings. Public use of some areas will be restricted for safety.

title: Pet Restrictions, Beach Driving Closures in Effect March 15 through Labor Day
description: To protect threatened nesting shorebirds, pets are prohibited in the Otis Pike Wilderness and on federally-managed ocean beaches. Beach driving is closed at Lighthouse Beach, Sailors Haven and the Wilderness area.

title: Delays along Highway 101
description: There are multiple traffic stops along Highway 101 from Orick, CA to Crescent City, CA due to road construction. Extra time may be needed to travel throughout the park. Delay times may vary. Please stay alert and drive cautiously.

title: 6/16/26 - 8/6/26 Roadside Vegetation Removal - Expect Short Traffic Delays
description: Vegetation crews will be removing encroaching plants along Rim Rock Drive to increase roadside visibility for drivers. Crews will start at the west entrance headed eastbound, and traffic will be reduced to one lane in sections where the crew is working. Vehicles may be stopped temporarily, but delays should last no more than 10 minutes at a time.

title: Ryan Visitor Center Phone Line Out of Service
description: The Floyd Bennett Field Ryan Visitor Center phone line (718-338-3799) is out of service. For information on ranger programs in the Jamaica Bay Unit, call the Jamaica Bay Wildlife Refuge Visitor Center at 718-318-4340. For questions about permits, events, or other park information, call the general park information line at 718-354-4606. For emergencies, call U.S. Park Police's 24-hour dispatch at 718-354-4700.

title: Barataria Visitor Center and Trails are Closed
description: Because of upcoming demolition and construction of the trails and Visitor Center, all trails at the Barataria Preserve and the Visitor Center are closed, with the exception of Twin Canals Trail. This is a day-use area only with no restrooms. Visitor services are relocated to the Wetlands Education Center and trails at 4917 City Park Drive, Jean Lafitte, 70067. Rangers will be on site Wednesdays and Thursdays 10 am to 2 pm for programming and ranger talks at the Town of Lafitte's Civic Center.

title: Road work at Oregon Caves
description: A pavement resurfacing project is taking place in the parking lots and campground at Oregon Caves. Repaving will be occurring Monday-Friday from 8am-6pm. Please allow some extra time while traveling to and from Oregon Caves.

title: Battery 234 Loop Road Closure
description: The Battery 234 Loop Road and Battery Cooper within the GUIS, Fort Pickens Management Area will be closed to all for vehicle, bicyclists, and foot (pedestrian) traffic until further notice for safety purposes until the park can correct the leaning and structurally unstable historic Tower 234 that poses danger to visitors and staff. The beach access points for pedestrians from the Gulf (south) side will also be closed. The pipe gates at the entrance and exit points will be locked with accompanied signage.

title: Broken Windsock at Serpentine Hot Springs
description: The windsock at the Serpentine Hot Springs airstrip is broken, and the National Park Service is in the process of ordering a replacement. At this time, we do not have an estimated date for when it will be reinstalled. Please use caution when utilizing the airstrip.

title: Glenmont Heat Advisory
description: The house at Glenmont is currently experiencing high heat conditions. As a result, house tours may be abbreviated or canceled due to safety concerns.

title: Tisch Mills Segment — Seasonal Flooding
description: The Ice Age Trail from Mill Road to Nuclear Road is often flooded in spring or after heavy rain. To bypass this section, follow CTH-B between CTH-BB and Nuclear Road.

title: Hot Conditions
description: Limit strenuous hiking to early morning and late evening hours. Expect temperatures in the High Peaks and Chalone Peak to be at least 10 degrees hotter than parking areas. Drink plenty of water and carry at least one liter of water for each hour of hiking. Bring salty snacks, a hat, and sunscreen for the hike. Know the signs and symptoms of heat related illnesses. In case of a heat related emergency get to a cool place and seek help immediately.

title: Vehicle Break-Ins
description: Vehicle break-ins have occurred at the King Canyon Trailhead, as well as at other trailheads throughout the park. Hide valuables and consider taking them with you, secure your vehicle, and report any suspicious activity. Please call 911 to report criminal activity or the Pima County Sherriff's Department Non-Emergency number at 520-351-4900.

title: Reds Meadow Road Access Restrictions in 2026
description: Reds Meadow Road remains under construction in 2026 and will be closed Monday through Friday from June 13 through July 1, then Monday through Wednesday from July 2 through September 20, then Monday through Friday starting September 21.

title: Being Prepared for Excessive Heat & Humidity
description: Congaree can be hot & humid from late spring through early fall. Be sure that you & your party (including pets) have adequate water & choose activities that fit your level of physical fitness. Consider visiting early in the morning when it is cooler.

title: Fire restrictions in place
description: Fire restrictions are in place at Mojave National Preserve and Castle Mountains National Monument. Wood and charcoal fires are not permitted. Most camp stoves are. See fire restriction order for additional details.

title: Fire restrictions in place
description: Fire restrictions are in place at Mojave National Preserve and Castle Mountains National Monument. Wood and charcoal fires are not permitted. Most camp stoves are. See fire restriction order for additional details.

title: I-70 Closure in Downtown Topeka May Affect Travel to the Park
description: I-70 is closed through downtown Topeka between Topeka Boulevard and 8th Avenue due to construction. Visitors traveling to Brown v. Board of Education National Historical Park should allow extra travel time and follow posted detours. Westbound visitors may continue on I-70 and follow signs to local exits near downtown Topeka. Eastbound visitors should use I-470 around Topeka, then connect to local streets to reach the park at 1515 SE Monroe Street. Check KanDrive.gov or call 511 for current road condition

title: EV charging station unavailable
description: The Electric Vehicle charging station is non-functional. There is no timeline for when it may become available. Please plan accordingly.

title: Temporary Wall Street Closures
description: Beginning Monday June 15, the Wall Street side of the Navajo Loop will be closed Monday - Thursday from 6 AM to 12 Noon for critical trail stabilization work. The Two Bridges side of the Navajo Loop will remain open. This work will continue through the 2026 season.

title: Old Springs Trail near Tennessee Valley Closed until August 2026
description: The trail will be closed for boardwalk replacement and general maintenance until early August. Surrounding trails will remain open to provide an alternative route. Please pay attention to safety signage and stay out of the closed area.

title: OSV Status
description: 6/8/26 MD open to State Line. VA South OSV fully closed. The VA North OSV fishing mile is open to 12 vehicles.

title: Fire Restrictions in Place
description: Stage 1 Fire Restrictions are in effect. Wood and charcoal fires are prohibited at all low-elevation campgrounds and picnic areas. Additional restrictions apply. Click "more" for details.

title: Hours Changing
description: The Visitor Center at Friendship Hill National Historic Site is now open seven days a week from 9 AM to 5 PM! The grounds and trails remain open sunrise to sunset. If you have any questions, please give us a call at 724-329-2501 or visit our website at www.nps.gov/frhi

title: Photo Season
description: Just a reminder as the weather is starting to get nice, and people are thinking about where to take graduation, wedding, prom or formal, pregnancy, birthday, and any other type of photography or filming! We do have rules and regulations on what is or is not allowed and whether or not you need a permit. Violations may be ticketed. Please check our website under Plan Your Visit, Permits and Reservations!!! https://www.nps.gov/frhi/planyourvisit/permits.htm

title: Large vehicle restrictions now in effect for Zion-Mt. Carmel Highway
description: As of June 7, 2026, the park is enforcing size and weight limits for vehicles on the Zion-Mt. Carmel Highway. Vehicles that exceed length, width, height, or weight limits cannot travel between Canyon Junction and the park's East Entrance. See the current limits on the page linked below.

title: Lindenwald Opens for 2026 Season
description: Lindenwald Tours – 2026 Season Lindenwald is open for tours Friday–Sunday at 10 AM, 11 AM, 1 PM, and 3 PM. Tours are first-come, first-served. Monday–Thursday: grounds are open, but no tours are available. Park stamps, and restrooms are available in the Visitor Center.

title: Lassen National Park Highway Open for the 2026 Season
description: The Lassen National Park Highway (Hwy. 89, 30 miles through the park) opened to through traffic on May 22, 2026. Google maps and other third-party sites may be indicating the road is closed. This does not reflect accurate information.

title: Kahuku Unit Roads
description: Kahuku Road beyond the cross fence (mile marker 4) is closed to vehicles; pedestrian use is permitted. Four-wheel drive is strongly recommended past the Upper Palm Trailhead (mile marker 3).

title: Parking Lot E Closed for Construction
description: Parking Lot E is closed for construction. The park is currently working to expand this parking area, and the lot will be closed while the expansion is being built. Visitors can still access the Mary Byrd Branch Trail and Quantico Cascades Trail by following trail reroute signs and parking vehicles in Turkey Run parking area. For your safety, please follow all closures and only park in designated parking spots.

title: Road workers on Park Road in Davis Bayou
description: Phase II of the Davis Bayou Bicycle and Pedestrian Path is in process. Visitors may encounter minor traffic delays and flaggers on Eagle Point and Park Road.

title: Fredericksburg Battlefield Visitor Center Closed, Store and Grounds Open
description: Starting November 20, 2025 the Fredericksburg Battlefield Visitor Center will be closed while updates are made to building systems. Front Desk operations including visitor orientation will move to the adjacent Fredericksburg Battlefield Bookstore. The Chancellorsville Visitor Center remains open to visitors 9am - 5pm all week.

title: Ford's Theatre closed for Facility Upgrades June 3 - August 31, 2026
description: Ford's Theater and the Museum will temporarily close to public access on June 3, 2026, beginning at 9:00 a.m. The Theater will remain closed until July 31, 2026, at 9:00 a.m. The museum will remain closed until August 15, 2026, at 9:00 a.m. The Petersen House, the Center of Experiential Learning, and the Atlantic Lobby will remain open to the public. National Park Service staff will be available at these locations to provide site tours and visitor information.
